differences.what: Massing, six storeys to the cornice, the Randolph and Clark Street fronts' bay groups and the arcaded ground storey
The first-floor gallery's railing: the photograph shows a light iron railing, and the model now builds it open, rails, bars and posts, where it was a solid dark band
The third-floor balcony over the middle four bays of the Randolph front, now built with its open iron railing
The attic belvedere's stone balustrade on top, now built with its piers and balusters
The Clark Street portico: its columns now stand heavier, on plinths under capitals, carrying a deeper entablature and an open railed balcony
Awnings, signs, telegraph poles and carriages
The statue on the belvedere's corner and the attic's height, a little taller in the model than the photograph reads

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
